sections.heading: Praising you for choosing and saving me
sections.text: Holy Trinity—Father, Son, and Spirit—I praise you for saving me before I ever reached for you. Father, you knew me and set your love on me. Spirit, you are making me holy and teaching me to obey. Lord Jesus, your blood has cleansed me and brought me near. This is mercy beyond what I can explain, and I worship you for it.
theological_themes: God's saving work is Trinitarian: the Father elects, the Spirit sanctifies, and the Son cleanses by his blood.
Salvation begins in God's grace, not in human merit or initiative.
Obedience is the fruit and direction of God's saving work, not the ground of being accepted.

scripture_references.connection: Peter describes believers as chosen according to the Father's foreknowledge, sanctified by the Spirit, and brought into obedience and cleansing through Jesus Christ. This closely grounds the prayer's Trinitarian praise for election and salvation.
Paul blesses God for choosing his people in Christ and adopting them according to his gracious purpose. The passage supports thanking God for salvation as an act of undeserved, eternal grace.

sections.heading: Asking to know the privilege of belonging to you
sections.text: I am amazed that you do not keep me at a distance. You come to live with your people, and you bring them into fellowship with you. I believe this is true, but I do not want it to stay only as words in my head. Help me know it more deeply, trust it more steadily, and live as someone who is truly at home with you.
theological_themes: Believers are brought into communion with God, not merely forgiven from afar.
God's indwelling presence is a real privilege of the Christian life.
Faith asks God to make objective truth increasingly known and lived.

scripture_references.connection: Jesus promises that the Father and Son will make their home with those who love him. This supports the prayer's wonder that God draws near to dwell with his people.

John connects assurance of abiding in God with the Spirit's gift and with faith in God's love revealed in Christ. This helps frame the prayer's request to experience more fully the reality already confessed.

sections.heading: Resting my peace on Christ, not on myself
sections.text: Keep teaching me that my peace with you does not stand on how strong I feel today. It stands on Jesus. His righteousness answers your justice, and his cross shows your love. Help me take hold of him by faith as the sure ground of my acceptance with you. Keep me close to the cross, where I see both the seriousness of my sin and the fullness of your mercy.
theological_themes: Christ's righteousness, not personal performance or emotional condition, is the believer's ground of peace with God.
The cross displays both divine justice and divine love.
Faith receives and rests on what Christ has accomplished.

scripture_references.connection: Paul teaches that God justifies sinners through faith in Jesus Christ while showing both righteousness and mercy through Christ's blood. This grounds the prayer's claim that Christ satisfies justice and secures acceptance.

Paul rejects a righteousness of his own and seeks the righteousness from God that comes through faith in Christ. This supports the prayer's reliance on Christ's righteousness as the basis of peace with God.

sections.heading: Trusting what Christ has done more than what I feel
sections.text: Do not let me confuse passing feelings with the proof that I belong to you. Feelings can be mistaken, and spiritual impressions can deceive me if they are cut loose from your Word. Teach me to look first to the finished work of Christ, received by faith and confirmed by your Word and Spirit. What Jesus has done perfectly is stronger than my best day, my worst day, or anything I can sense inside myself.
theological_themes: Assurance rests fundamentally on Christ's finished work and God's testimony, not on fluctuating inward experience.
The Word and the Spirit together bear witness to the truth of the gospel.
Faith lays hold of Christ's death as personally saving without making feelings the foundation.

scripture_references.connection: Hebrews emphasizes that Christ's single offering has decisively sanctified and perfected those who belong to him. This supports the prayer's confidence in Christ's completed work rather than inner sensation.

John points believers to God's testimony concerning his Son so that they may know they have eternal life. This fits the prayer's insistence that assurance must be grounded in God's revealed witness, not unsupported impressions.

sections.heading: Leaving my life in your hands
sections.text: Thank you for giving me faith that can keep coming back to Jesus. Thank you that his righteousness is mine, and that you are teaching me to give up my will to yours. Everything that concerns me is in your hands, and I am glad to leave it there. When I remember that, my prayer becomes praise. I do not need human approval to hold me up. Your choosing grace is better, stronger, and more lasting than the favour of anyone else.
theological_themes: Faith leads to gratitude, worship, and surrender to God's will.
God's sovereign care frees the believer from anxious dependence on human approval.
Electing grace gives a deeper security than social acceptance or worldly support.

scripture_references.connection: Paul connects God's purpose, foreknowledge, calling, justification, and glorification, giving believers confidence that their lives are held within God's saving plan. This supports the prayer's glad surrender to God's disposal of all things.
Paul contrasts serving Christ with living for human approval. This illuminates the prayer's desire not to lean on the favour of people when God's grace is the believer's true security.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The doctrine of election is central to the original and is doctrinally contested among Christian traditions, especially regarding the nature of foreknowledge, divine choice, and human response. The adaptation preserves the original's Reformed emphasis without expanding it beyond the prayer's own claims.

The line about Christ's holiness or righteousness being made the believer's 'as if I had done it' reflects imputed righteousness. I rendered this in terms of Christ's righteousness being the ground of acceptance, while avoiding language that could imply believers personally performed Christ's obedience.

The original contrasts inward spiritual feeling with the objective work of Christ. I preserved that contrast while avoiding the implication that the Spirit's inward witness is unimportant; the adaptation places assurance in Christ's work as testified by the Word and Spirit.
significant_interpretive_choices: I treated 'all heaven comes to dwell' as a statement about God's indwelling presence and communion with the believer, not as a literal spatial claim about heaven.

I rendered 'make use of it by faith' as actively relying on Christ's righteousness for peace and acceptance, because the original is concerned with faith appropriating Christ's finished work rather than merely knowing doctrine abstractly.
I interpreted 'all things are at thy disposal' as glad surrender to God's sovereign care over one's life, not fatalism or passivity.
